Figure 2:Overview of GlyphAtlas.
GlyphAtlas conditions a DiT on two complementary glyph references:
(1) the glyph image, which is spatially aligned with the scene and anchors the layout and coarse glyph structure of every text region;
(2) the glyph atlas, which renders each character or word in a separate cell at a resolution independent of its target region and supplies fine-grained stroke references.
Atlas-anchored attention binds the two through an attention mask, so that each text region retrieves stroke detail only from its own atlas cells.

Figure 3:Demonstration of the glyph atlas construction.
The height of atlas cell can be adjusted to control the atlas token budget.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on evaluated benchmarks.
Gray marks the regions to be filled.
More comparisons are in the supplementary.
“GT” is the abbreviation for Ground Truth, and all columns of a row show the same crop.
